description:
FILED s488a (Opus, 2026-09-17) while reading the companion bar for task #1834.

Every `--all` companion run reports a large ROW DIFF that is NOT a regression:
s488a measured 396 NEW ROW / 536 FIXED ROW over nine files, and the NEW and
FIXED counts are EQUAL per file for most of them (re/regexp_normal.t 128/128,
re/charset.t 104/104, re/subst.t 14/14, re/subst_amp.t 12/12,
re/pat_rt_report.t 4/4, op/lex.t 1/1) -- the SAME rows leaving and entering,
because the baseline holds their KEY in a spelling the runner's current
projection no longer produces.

MEASURED PRE-EXISTING, not caused by the batch: a `git archive main`
extraction run with `--jobs 1 op/lex.t re/subst_amp.t` reports the same
13 NEW / 13 FIXED, the same rows both ways.

TWO SPELLINGS, both visible in one run:
  * a NON-ASCII description.  op/lex.t's blessed key is
      Various tests of string delims \xAB/\xBB returned without error
    and the run's log carries the RAW BYTES of the same description
    (Â«/Â», which a byte-oriented reader renders as U+FFFD).  One of the two was
    written under a different encoding assumption; they are the same row.
  * the `[at FILE line N]` fallback for an UNNAMED test.  re/subst_amp.t's
    twelve rows key as `[at t/re/subst_amp.t line 22]` now, and the baseline
    carries the other spelling.  `PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc($desc, $tdir)`
    normalises the perl-suite t/ directory out of a description, so a row
    blessed before that normalisation (or from a run with a different $tdir)
    keys differently -- the same trap s473t5c's f3a2c4a6 fixed for a HAND
    splice ("a hand splice needs the runner's WHOLE key projection").

WHY IT MATTERS: the ROW DIFF block is one of the three the runner asks you to
read, and ~400 permanent false NEW rows make it unreadable -- a REAL new
failing row has to be spotted beside them.  It is the same reading failure
#1834 fixed for the SNAPSHOT block, and s488a fixed exactly ONE row of it by
hand (op/inccode-tie.t, whose key was the message TEXT where the projection
answers `*summary*`).

THE FIX (one-time, and #1835 now makes it safe): re-key the affected files'
blocks THROUGH the current projection and splice them back per file, carrying
each row's CAUSE by its old key -- which is what `bless_fail_rows` already does
(it re-attaches `$blessed_fail_cause{"$rel\t$key"}`) and what
`PCLBaseline::splice_blocks` keeps to the measured blocks.  So the mechanical
step is a `--bless-fails` run over JUST those files, with the diff READ row by
row to confirm that every line is a re-key and nothing else moves.  Do NOT
re-bless the whole baseline: the causes of rows the run did not measure would
be at risk, and that is the very thing #1835 stopped.

ENTRY BAR before doing it: the count of affected rows must first be measured
per file on a main extraction (s488a measured two files; the run names nine),
because a file whose rows moved for a REAL reason must not ride along.
subject: the companion ROW DIFF reports ~396 NEW / ~536 FIXED rows on every run that are the SAME rows re-keyed: the baseline holds a non-ASCII description escaped (`\xAB`) and an `[at FILE line N]` fallback in a spelling the current projection does not produce (measured identically on a main extraction)
